channel.title: The Git Reporter
channel.description: The Git Reporter is a software newspaper for developers, builders, and curious readers, explaining changes through public code and source evidence.

item.title: Ollama Adds D3 as OpenAI Expands Its Decisions API
item.description: Developers have another downloadable model for judging documents and images locally. Alongside OpenAI's now generally available Decisions API, it makes two choices clearer: where evidence is processed, and which work can be reused.

item.title: Phonon’s Offline Speech Is Now a Kit You Can Download
item.description: Gradium has opened a practical route from an app’s text to locally generated speech: download the runtime, model and a reusable voice. Preparing a new voice is a separate job.

item.title: DeepSeek opens the engine and the API adapter. What can you actually run?
item.description: DeepInfer exposes serious serving machinery. deepseek-recipe makes its API semantics portable. Getting the model onto a laptop follows a different path through quantization, system memory and SSD storage.

item.title: Pydantic Updates Agent Instructions Without Rewriting the Opening
item.description: An agent’s task state can change without changing the start of its next model request. Pydantic AI’s new append mode puts the update at the end of the conversation, preserving the earlier prefix for possible cache reuse.

item.title: RevEngine makes the review queue programmable
item.description: Laude’s open-source reviewer leads ReviewBench. Its newest code tackles a different problem: an automated reviewer must remember what a maintainer already decided without overlooking the next defect.

item.title: Vercel gives coding agents a life beyond one process
item.description: The new durable-harness package lets existing agents recover from a saved work record. Its most useful distinction is between work that finished, work that never started and work whose outcome needs checking.

item.title: OpenAI Gives 20 Languages the Same Database Exam
item.description: MultiLangBench asks a model to build a database engine in a chosen language. The revealing part is the examiner: reference SQLite reads the file that implementation leaves behind.

item.title: Unsloth Can Reject a New Model to Keep Another Loaded
item.description: New Studio code gives chat, image and video models a choice: share GPU memory when possible, make room, or refuse a disruptive load. When media does displace chat, it can also save the primary GGUF model’s cached work.

item.title: Watching Codex Can Change When Its Tools Start
item.description: New request observers expose outcomes and available token usage. Where you put them in the sequence changes when a tool can leave the queue.

item.title: Pi Can Park Agent Tasks Until the Host Wakes Them
item.description: Pi’s experimental durable harness now stores a sleeping task’s deadline and next step, letting a host alarm bring execution back later. The change separates continuing work from a continuously running process.

item.title: Goose Replaces V8 Without Giving Up Tool Batching
item.description: The agent’s development branch swaps PCTX’s Deno-based runtime for Boa. It keeps the ability to discover tools and compose their results, while removing generated TypeScript and a chain of build workarounds.

item.title: Gemini CLI Now Sends Gemini 4 Users to Antigravity
item.description: Google’s open-source terminal agent now warns that it is not optimized for Gemini 4 Argon. The recommendation makes its direction clearer while fresh implementation fixes show a project still being maintained.

item.title: How Codex made the assignment the center of the app
item.description: Every’s origin story celebrates a desktop built around agents. The public record reveals the quieter achievement underneath: separating the machinery that does the work from the interface that helps people direct it.

item.title: QM Drops Two Agent Loops but Keeps ChatGPT Access
item.description: The shared workplace agent is narrowing its runtime choices to Pi and Claude. Its October 14 code change shows why keeping a model connection does not require keeping the agent software that shares its name.

item.title: Gemini’s Longer Answers Now Span Multiple Requests
item.description: Google’s Argon can continue a response beyond one request’s output limit. Pydantic AI’s released integration shows what that means for an agent: one answer, several network calls, and two different ways of counting tokens.

item.title: Ollama Opens Another Local Path for Image and Audio Search
item.description: A new prerelease carries media through Ollama’s llama-server backend, alongside its existing MLX route. Google’s EmbeddingGemma 2 supplies the shared representations; applications still decide what to index and how to search it.

item.title: How Grep AgentRun turns repeated agent work into decision workflows
item.description: Its open workflow engine can keep the procedure, ask a model for bounded judgments and call an agent only when investigation is needed. The useful comparison separates the value of reusable code from the value of the decision model.

item.title: Hermes Puts Assembled Agent Instructions into Code Review
item.description: A new snapshot shows reviewers the system prompt and tool definitions produced by the code. Nine controlled configurations turn changes in the agent’s instructions into something maintainers can compare directly.

item.title: Unsloth Adds Shared Fine-Tuning for Seven Text-Diffusion Families
item.description: A new trainer connects familiar datasets to distinct learning recipes for models that refine text instead of only predicting the next token. The gain is less custom integration—and a clearer view of the differences that still matter.

item.title: Unsloth Adds Chosen MCP Sources to Research Reports
item.description: Studio’s research mode can draw on search tools you select, alongside the web and its knowledge base. The merged change expands what can reach a report, while leaving a revealing boundary around how the next question is chosen.

item.title: Pi and Crush Tell the Terminal When They Need You
item.description: Two released coding agents now share a status protocol for working, waiting and finished runs. It gives compatible terminals a way to surface the agent that needs attention—without deciphering each tool’s screen.

item.title: Pi Adds Screenshot Questions to Its Classifier Interface
item.description: Pi 1.1.0 lets an agent script send images to OpenAI Decisions and receive answers it can use in code. The release expands a practical division of labor: the main model writes the task, a separate call judges a bounded question, and the script chooses what happens next.

item.title: A Fast Model Can Send the Agent Back to Ask
item.description: Strands puts a small decision model between an agent's proposed action and its tool. Browser and document experiments reveal a wider division of labor: models judge, software defines the choices, and escalation can mean another model—or a person.

item.title: Goose Keeps Parallel Agents, Drops the Collect-Later Workflow
item.description: An October 7 change removes background task handles from Goose while preserving concurrent helpers. The distinction matters for anyone whose recipes ask an agent to start work, carry on, and collect the answer later.

item.title: Figma Changes Can Wake a Waiting Pi Agent
item.description: A new extension brings design feedback into a running agent without another terminal prompt. Its public code exposes the handoff; an author-reported live test carries it through to a canvas revision.

item.title: OpenWork Can Import Your Cowork Plugins and Skill Instructions
item.description: A new migration command finds existing setup, previews the move and imports selected plugins. The useful change is less work to try another assistant—with a precise boundary around what travels.

item.title: Direct Reports Drive Anthropic’s Growing Vulnerability Count
item.description: The company’s disclosure total has more than doubled since August. Most of the net increase sits in the route without the same external review—a useful distinction when judging what the expanding program delivers.

item.title: Hugging Face Adds Task-by-Task Browsing for Agent Benchmarks
item.description: Harbor’s executable tests now fit the ordinary dataset viewer and loading tools. Evaluators can inspect instructions and declared requirements together before choosing which work to run.

item.title: Git Adds Squashing Without Switching Branches
item.description: The experimental history editor can fold an older patch series while leaving a separate working branch alone. Its handling of dependent branches—and some merges—defines the useful new choice.

item.title: ChatGPT Plugins Can Now Start Work from App Events
item.description: OpenAI’s new event subscriptions give plugin builders a way to describe what should start a job. The useful change is an explicit integration contract for ongoing work, with the app still responsible for getting its events delivered.
